hypothesis: The strategy that the frozen engine picks using only data up to the start of a block makes money after cost in that block.
null_H0: For every block b: E[X_b | everything known before block b starts] <= 0, where X_b is the realised net P&L of block b as a fraction of the capital given to the block (after cost, funding, the in-block stop and the margin floor).
why_this_null: The e-process below is valid under this conditional-mean null whatever the dependence, volatility clustering or right tail of returns (Waudby-Smith & Ramdas 2010.09686 Prop. 2-3; Ville). It does NOT need i.i.d. blocks or a model of returns. It needs a LOWER bound on X_b, which is why the stop and the margin floor are part of the hypothesis.

blocks.length: one calendar month (28-31 days; the simulation used 30)
blocks.first_block_decided: 2026-12-01 (DECIDED 2026-10-22 by 동동, "그대로 진행"). Engine, bundle rule and this file must be frozen and committed with sha256 before it.
blocks.warmup: the block tool reads 60 days strictly before the block start for feature warm-up; entries only inside the block; an entry whose holding period does not end inside the block is not taken (evaluator rule: exit must be inside the read bars), so every block starts and ends flat
blocks.no_end_date: the e-process may be monitored after every block and stopped at any time; the error rate holds for any stopping rule (anytime-valid). A block's X_b is booked once, after the block ends, and is never revised.
blocks.booking: a block is booked once, in order, after its last day and after Binance publishes its monthly files (normally within the first days of the next month), with run/evalue_v3_block.py block (ACTIVE prereg only). A booked X_b is never revised.

pipeline.engine: pinned in the members file: code.code_hash = prereg_gate.research_code_identity() (DEV pipeline + evaluator files), code.v3_code_sha256 = evalue_v3.v3_code_sha256() (run/discovery/evalue_v3.py + run/evalue_v3_block.py), context_id of the DEV-only state directory. prereg_gate checks the first and evalue_v3.check_members the second before any block is evaluated; a change of either ends the family (no_human_choice).
pipeline.rerun_rule: the draft said: rerun the DEV-only search at each block start on data up to the day before. With the frozen engine this gives the SAME candidates every block, because the engine's DEV reads end at fixed dates (each symbol's validation window and the refused reads of strong_search_dev; anything from 2025-10-21 is refused). Letting it read the new months would read ETH validation / locked TEST / paper data, which is forbidden. So the members are frozen once and the same bundle is traded in every block; at each block the tool re-checks the members file hash and both code pins instead of rerunning. The test is still one hypothesis: this bundle makes money after cost, block after block.
pipeline.no_human_choice: no person may change the engine, the candidate list, the cost profile, the sizing or the selection between blocks. A change ends this family; the e-value at that moment is reported as the final result, and any new design is a new family with its own alpha.
pipeline.flat_block: if the selection rule picks nothing, X_b = 0 for that block (factor 1, no evidence either way)

bundle.weights: equal; fewer than 5 eligible -> the eligible ones equally weighted, none -> flat block (X_b = 0)
bundle.why: same unit as v2 D3; spreads single-rule noise (ADR 0021: bundles cut volatility); the e-process still tests ONE hypothesis (the pipeline's bundle)

pipeline.members_rule: take pipeline.validation_candidates() of ONE DEV-only evolve state directory run on the frozen code (default candidate selection config, one per entry signal, ADR 0031/0033), in its own order; the members are the first pipeline.bundle.members (5) of that list. No entry bar (v3 has none). Each member's rule is applied to every universe symbol. Frozen with run/evalue_v3_block.py freeze, then dev-scale seals the vol scale into the same file.

sizing_and_bounds.vol_target: scale k such that the bundle's DEV daily volatility is vol_target_daily of the block capital
sizing_and_bounds.stop_rule: if the block's running net P&L reaches -L, close everything and stay flat until the block ends
sizing_and_bounds.floor_rule: isolated margin of B: a gap through the stop cannot lose more than B of the block capital; the paper evaluation books max(value, -B) and records the raw value
sizing_and_bounds.gap_allowance_reason: the margin floor hands the trader the part of a gap below -B, so a no-skill strategy can show a slightly positive mean (simulated: up to +0.066 % per block with GJR + skewed t3 tails, +0.023 % with skewed t4); c = 0.27 % is 4x the worst simulated bias and 12x the t4 bias
sizing_and_bounds.units: all three numbers are fractions of the block capital; they are fixed here, not estimated later
sizing_and_bounds.scale_rule: DEV series = equal-weight mean over members of the basket-average daily net bp (exit-day booking, the v2 statistic) on the DEV stretch S1 of run/forward_v2_entry_bar_dev.py (2021-04-01..2023-09-18, same refused reads), with this file's cost; k = vol_target_daily * 1e4 / sd(series), capped at scale_max; computed once at freeze (run/evalue_v3_block.py dev-scale) and sealed in the members file. Block P&L fraction = k * bundle bp / 1e4.
sizing_and_bounds.scale_max_reason: a member that is rarely in the market has a tiny DEV volatility; without a cap k would put very large notional on a few trades
sizing_and_bounds.stop_check: at every UTC day-end of the block: closed events count their net bp, open events are marked at the last 15m close before the day-end minus their whole round-trip cost and their funding pro rata. The first day-end at or below -stop_L closes everything at that value and the block is flat afterwards. The simulation stepped daily too.

e_process.bet_rule: Waudby-Smith & Ramdas (2010.09686 v7) hedged-capital BETTING PRODUCT (Theorem 3, one-sided K+): capital prod(1 + lam_b Z_b) with the predictable plug-in bet of eq. (15)/(26), in Z units, no prior on the edge (wording corrected 2026-10-22, ADR 0032: this was called 'PrPl-EB', but the paper's PrPl-EB is the exponential supermartingale of Theorem 2, a different and much weaker rule; formula, code and numbers are unchanged): lam_b = min(sqrt(2 * ln(2 / alpha) / (s2_{b-1} * b * ln(1 + b))), 0.75), alpha = 0.0091; s2_0 = s0^2, s2_t = (s0^2 + sum_{i<=t} (Z_i - mu_i)^2) / (t + 1), mu_t = sum_{i<=t} Z_i / (t + 1), s0 = block_sd / (B + c). Code: run/evalue_walkforward_sim.py log_e_hedged_prpl_bet (alias log_e_prpl_eb, alpha=0.0091). Changed 2026-10-22 (ADR 0030, decision V3)
e_process.bet_rule_previous: predictable plug-in: lam_b = clip(mu / (v + mu^2), 0, 0.75) with mu = sum(Z_1..Z_{b-1}) / (b - 1 + 3) and v = (3 * s0^2 + sum Z_i^2) / (b - 1 + 3) (replaced: same type I, lower power; ADR 0027)
e_process.E_b: product of the factors of blocks 1..b (E_0 = 1)
e_process.prior_from_spent_windows: NOT USED for the bet (decision V3). Spent BTC/ETH windows and DEV overstate Sharpe by about 3-5x (ADR 0021: H1 1.9-2.5 -> H2 0.44-0.90); simulated 5x overestimate lost half the power at true SR 3; the eq. (15) bet uses no estimate of the edge at all.
e_process.breach: if a realised X_b < -B ever occurs (margin floor failed, e.g. ADL or exchange failure), the family is VOID: no rejection may be claimed from that block on, and the breach is reported
e_process.code: run/discovery/evalue_v3.py e_path (same rule as run/evalue_walkforward_sim.py log_e_hedged_prpl_bet; checked equal in run/test_evalue_v3.py)
